correctness.rationale: I inspected the complete RESULT.md and the actual standard-library verify.py at the frozen source blob. The graph has 24 vertices and 37 edges. The checker builds every matching as a 37-bit mask; I independently reconstructed the monomer–dimer column-transfer dynamic program and obtained all 1,222,549 faces, with the exact claimed f-vector (37,584,5161,28191,99183,227262,335396,308330,165871,46801,5580,153) and reduced Euler characteristic -94. The source constructs a deterministic sequence of pivot-edge matchings on the entire nonempty face poset, checks disjoint pairing and exact counts 611,209 pairs/131 critical cells, and verifies acyclicity by a topological sort of all 8,827,379 oriented Hasse incidences. This is the crucial nonheuristic Morse hypothesis, not merely a count of critical cells. The remaining CW model has one degree-zero, 112 degree-seven and 18 degree-eight critical cells. The gradient-path recursion defines the signed 112x18 integral differential; the specified 182-entry ±1 matrix admits 18 unimodular unit pivots, hence primitive image and zero degree-eight homology. As the 7-skeleton is a wedge of 7-spheres and Hurewicz isomorphism identifies all 8-cell attaching maps with their integer degree vectors, the unit reduction cancels 18 sphere pairs, leaving 94 S7 wedges. The nontrivial million-face Hasse/Differential certificate code was read and evaluated logically, not fully re-executed in this environment; the independent exact f-vector check is narrower than the full homotopy theorem. No generalization to arbitrary widths is inferred.

value.rationale: The exact integral homotopy type of a canonical 3xn grid at n=8 is a natural finite classification and sharp test of whether the ordinary matching complex is a single-degree sphere wedge. A complete acyclic matching plus primitive attaching differential resolves information that connectivity or Betti data alone cannot provide, particularly after a claimed general wedge classification was retracted. It is independently useful as a width-eight benchmark; no paper-sized or all-width theorem is required.
